title: AgentLTV: An Agent-Based Unified Search-and-Evolution Framework for Automated Lifetime Value Prediction

mechanism.populationDetail: The first stage maintains an explicit tree of executable pipeline programs, and the second stage maintains multiple persistent island populations seeded from the best MCTS program.
mechanism.archiveDetail: Each EA island retains a top fitness-ranked elite subset for later reproduction and migration; no descriptor-cell archive is specified.
mechanism.replacementDetail: MCTS appends evaluated child nodes to a persistent tree, while EA forms each next generation from retained elites plus offspring and migrates high-fitness elites across islands.
mechanism.generationDetail: MCTS roots are generated without a parent, MCTS expansions broadly modify one selected tree program, and EA explicitly combines multiple elite parents through crossover followed by unary mutation.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Code Fixer execution/repair results and multi-metric scores are fed into MCTS priors/rewards and EA advice; repair retries are not automatically repeated evaluation of an unchanged candidate.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: MCTS selects one expansion node by PUCT; EA selects high-fitness elite parents within each island, uses multiple parents for crossover and one parent for mutation, and then migrates elites across islands.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: A sequential MCTS-tree-to-island-EA handoff combines tree-statistic control, multi-parent crossover, and island migration in one system; current fields do not represent all stage-specific parent cardinalities or this cross-stage controller cleanly.

provenance.citationWarning: Keep tree and island placements separate; do not treat elite subsets as QD archives or advice/neighbor context as true parents. Multi-model subtype is unclear from the paper. The current survey cites AgentLTV in both state-independent and adaptive explore-exploit discussions because the fixed outer stage schedule and online PUCT control coexist. Repair retries should not be labeled repeated evaluation without stronger evidence.
